editorial.headline: Business Training, Open to Foreign Investment in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private providers can deliver business and management skills training at every listed scale, with national PMA openness up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Private business and management job training is practical skills education, not a generic advisory label. It covers privately delivered training designed to add business and management capability: secretarial work, office administration, ICT for secretaries, finance, commerce and sales, foreign languages, productivity promotion, consulting guidance, productivity measurement, productivity-improvement management, entrepreneurship and related subjects. The connecting idea is the deliberate transfer of work-ready expertise. These are disciplines through which organisations can administer, sell, measure performance and develop entrepreneurial capacity. A programme may be tightly specialised or span several subjects, but its stated purpose remains training that builds skills and expertise.

The registration frame is broad in business size. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the record does not reserve it for one type of provider. That accommodates a focused private operator as well as a larger training business offering a wider curriculum. Scale, however, does not change the activity’s essential character. The service being organised is job training in business and management, expressed through the subjects set out in its scope. That distinction keeps an expansive curriculum anchored to a clear practical purpose: helping participants add relevant skills or expertise.

Nationally, the investment position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%; in plain terms, national registration permits full foreign ownership. Bali does not reverse that conclusion for PMA registration today. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent island-wide moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this activity is expressly recorded outside that block. For a founder assessing Bali, the useful conclusion is precise: the activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
